subproblem.title: An integer multiplicity 2-cycle supported in finitely many 2-planes meeting at 0 has integer density at 0
subproblem.statement: Let P, q ∈ ℕ, let C ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P) be integer multiplicity with ∂C = 0 (BoundaryVanishes C), and let P_1, …, P_q (a family indexed by Fin q) be 2-dimensional linear subspaces of ℝ^P with P_i ∩ P_j = {0} (P_i ⊓ P_j = ⊥) for i ≠ j, such that every x ∈ spt C with x ≠ 0 lies in some P_i. Then there is m ∈ ℕ with HasMassDensity C 0 m, i.e. Θ²(μ_C, 0) = m.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P q : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 2) (Ps : Fin q → Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), IsIntegerMultiplicity C → BoundaryVanishes C → (∀ i, Module.finrank ℝ (Ps i) = 2) → (∀ i j, i ≠ j → Ps i ⊓ Ps j = ⊥) → (∀ x ∈ C.support, x ≠ 0 → ∃ i, x ∈ Ps i) → ∃ m : ℕ, HasMassDensity C 0 m
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 8 of the parent proof, i.e. the book's constancy argument (chapter-07.txt lines 505–510: "since Θ^n(S, ·) is constant on P_i ∖ {0} (by the Constancy 2.34 of Ch. 6), we have that Θ^n(S, y) ∈ ℤ"); step 0 of the parent proof (empty support) is the case q = 0 or all c_i = 0. Notation: H² = μHE[2]; ω_2 = unitBallVolume 2; M_W = massOn; B_r(x) = ball x r.
0. (Mass measure.) Fix an IMRep R of ℝ^P with R.Represents C and let μ := R.measure = (H²⌞R.carrier).withDensity(R.mult). By the accepted Submission.dimred_im_mass_measure (U := ℝ^P, open): (a) M_W(C) = μ(W) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P; (b) x ∈ spt C iff μ(B_ε(x)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0. μ is finite on compact sets (for compact K, μ(K) = ∫⁻_{R.carrier ∩ K} R.mult dH² ≠ ∞ by the field locallyIntegrable_mult), hence on bounded sets. H²({0}) = 0: by Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero_or_top (0 < 2), μHE[2]({0}) = 0 or μHE[0]({0}) = ∞, and μHE[0]({0}) = μH[0]({0}) = 1 (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero, hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton). Since μ is absolutely continuous with respect to H², μ({0}) = 0.
1. (The domains V_i.) Each P_i is closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional). For each i let V_i := ℝ^P ∖ ⋃_{j≠i} P_j, which is open as the complement of a finite union of closed sets. (i) P_i ∖ {0} ⊆ V_i: if x ∈ P_i ∩ P_j with j ≠ i, then x ∈ P_i ⊓ P_j = {0}. (ii) V_i ∩ P_i is connected (and nonempty): if q = 1, V_i = ℝ^P and V_i ∩ P_i = P_i, which is convex; if q ≥ 2, some j ≠ i exists and 0 ∈ P_j, so V_i ∩ P_i = P_i ∖ {0} by (i), the image of the connected set {0}ᶜ of the 2-dimensional space P_i (Mathlib isConnected_compl_singleton_of_one_lt_rank, rank P_i = 2 > 1) under the continuous inclusion P_i → ℝ^P. (iii) spt C ∩ V_i ⊆ P_i: let x ∈ spt C ∩ V_i. If x ≠ 0, x ∈ P_j for some j by hypothesis, and x ∉ P_j for j ≠ i, so x ∈ P_i. If x = 0, then 0 ∈ V_i forces that no j ≠ i exists (0 ∈ P_j for every j), and 0 ∈ P_i.
2. (Restrictions.) Let C_i := C.restrictDomain (V_i ⊆ ℝ^P) ∈ 𝒟_2(V_i), so C_i(ω) = C(ιω) with ι := testFormOnInclusion. (a) C_i is integer multiplicity by the accepted Submission.dtc_restrictDomain_isIntegerMultiplicity (V_i open). (b) BoundaryVanishes C_i: for ω ∈ 𝒟^1(V_i), ∂C_i(ω) = C_i(dω) = C(ι(dω)); the test forms ι(dω) and d(ιω) of ℝ^P have the same underlying form dω, so ∂C_i(ω) = C(d(ιω)) = ∂C(ιω) = 0. (c) spt C_i ⊆ P_i: let x ∈ V_i ∖ spt C. Then x lies in an open set W₀ with compact closure on which C vanishes; choose ε > 0 with closedBall(x, ε) ⊆ V_i. W := W₀ ∩ B_ε(x) is open, contains x, has compact closure contained in closedBall(x, ε) ⊆ V_i, and C_i vanishes on W (for ω ∈ 𝒟^2(V_i) with tsupport ω ⊆ W, C_i(ω) = C(ιω) = 0 since tsupport(ιω) = tsupport ω ⊆ W₀). So x lies in the zero region of C_i, i.e. x ∉ spt C_i. Hence spt C_i ⊆ spt C ∩ V_i ⊆ P_i by 1(iii). (d) M_W(C_i) = M_W(C) for every W ⊆ V_i: ω ↦ ιω is a bijection from the M_W-admissible forms of 𝒟^2(V_i) onto those of 𝒟^2(ℝ^P) (a form of 𝒟^2(ℝ^P) with tsupport ⊆ W ⊆ V_i belongs to 𝒟^2(V_i)) preserving underlying forms and values, so the two suprema coincide.
3. (Planar constancy.) Let τ^(i) : Fin 2 → ℝ^P be an orthonormal basis of P_i (stdOrthonormalBasis of P_i reindexed by Fin 2, as finrank P_i = 2, followed by the inclusion); it is orthonormal in ℝ^P and span(range τ^(i)) = P_i. The parent's sibling prerequisite Submission.idtp_planar_cycle_eq_const_mul (n := 2, V := V_i, S := C_i, τ := τ^(i)) applies by steps 1 and 2: 1 ≤ 2; V_i is open; τ^(i) is orthonormal; C_i is integer multiplicity; BoundaryVanishes C_i; spt C_i ⊆ P_i; V_i ∩ P_i is connected. It gives c_i ∈ ℤ with M_W(C_i) = |c_i|·H²(W ∩ P_i) for every open W ⊆ V_i. By 2(d) and 0(a), μ(W) = |c_i|·H²(W ∩ P_i) for every open W ⊆ V_i.
4. (Borel extension.) Let ν₁ := μ⌞V_i and ν₂ := |c_i|·(H²⌞(P_i ∩ V_i)). For every open O ⊆ ℝ^P, O ∩ V_i is open and contained in V_i, so ν₁(O) = μ(O ∩ V_i) = |c_i|·H²(O ∩ V_i ∩ P_i) = ν₂(O). The open balls B_k(0), k ∈ ℕ, increase to ℝ^P, and ν₁(B_k(0)) ≤ μ(B_k(0)) < ∞, ν₂(B_k(0)) ≤ |c_i|·H²(P_i ∩ B_k(0)) < ∞ (equal to |c_i|·ω_2·k² by the sibling idtp_tdc_subspace_ball_measure for k > 0; the ball is empty for k = 0). Open sets form a π-system generating the Borel σ-algebra, so ν₁ = ν₂ (Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.ext_of_generateFrom_of_iUnion). Hence μ(E) = ν₁(E) = ν₂(E) = |c_i|·H²(E ∩ P_i) for every Borel E ⊆ V_i.
5. (Null set off the planes.) O := ℝ^P ∖ ({0} ∪ ⋃_i P_i) is open and disjoint from spt C (every x ∈ spt C with x ≠ 0 lies in some P_i). By 0(b), every x ∈ O has ε_x > 0 with μ(B_{ε_x}(x)) = 0. Since ℝ^P is second countable, countably many of these balls cover O (TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable), so μ(O) = 0.
6. (Mass of the balls about 0.) Fix ρ > 0. The sets {0}, O and P_i ∖ {0} (i ∈ Fin q) are pairwise disjoint Borel sets ((P_i ∖ {0}) ∩ (P_j ∖ {0}) = ∅ for i ≠ j because P_i ⊓ P_j = ⊥) whose union is ℝ^P. As μ({0}) = μ(O) = 0, finite additivity gives μ(B_ρ(0)) = Σ_i μ(B_ρ(0) ∩ (P_i ∖ {0})). Each B_ρ(0) ∩ (P_i ∖ {0}) is a Borel subset of V_i by 1(i), so step 4 and H²({0}) = 0 give μ(B_ρ(0) ∩ (P_i ∖ {0})) = |c_i|·H²(B_ρ(0) ∩ (P_i ∖ {0})) = |c_i|·H²(P_i ∩ B_ρ(0)) = |c_i|·ω_2·ofReal(ρ²), the last equality by the sibling idtp_tdc_subspace_ball_measure (n := 2, y := 0 ∈ P_i). With m := Σ_i |c_i| ∈ ℕ (m = 0 if q = 0), 0(a) gives M_{B_ρ(0)}(C) = μ(B_ρ(0)) = m·ω_2·ofReal(ρ²).
7. (Density.) ω_2 = volume(ball (0 : Euclid 2) 1) ∈ (0, ∞) (a nonempty bounded open set) and ofReal(ρ²) ∈ (0, ∞) for ρ > 0, so M_{B_ρ(0)}(C)/(ω_2·ofReal(ρ²)) = m for every ρ > 0 (ENNReal.mul_div_cancel_right). Thus the ratio is eventually equal to m along 𝓝[>]0 and tends to (m : [0, ∞]) = ofReal(m). Since m ≥ 0, HasMassDensity C 0 m. ∎
proof_key_steps: On V_i = ℝ^P ∖ ⋃_{j≠i} P_j the restriction C_i is an integer multiplicity cycle with spt C_i ⊆ P_i, and V_i ∩ P_i (P_i or P_i ∖ {0}) is connected.
idtp_planar_cycle_eq_const_mul gives c_i ∈ ℤ with μ(W) = |c_i|·H²(W ∩ P_i) for open W ⊆ V_i, which extends to Borel subsets of V_i by π–λ uniqueness.
μ vanishes on {0} (H²({0}) = 0) and on the open set off the planes (it misses spt C).
Summing over the disjoint sets P_i ∖ {0} and using idtp_tdc_subspace_ball_measure gives M_{B_ρ(0)}(C) = (Σ|c_i|)·ω_2ρ² for every ρ > 0.
The density ratio is constantly m = Σ|c_i|, so HasMassDensity C 0 m.

audit.reason: Restriction preserves the required cycle, support, and mass properties. Connected punctured planes permit planar constancy; measure uniqueness extends the formula to Borel pieces. Null mass at the origin and off the planes then gives the constant integer density ratio, including q = 0. No cone or minimizing hypothesis is silently required.
